title: Handoff vignettes & tempo notes
content:
Purpose: quick, scannable handoff for midwatch -> nights. Not formal runbook — ephemeral checks and tempo notes I keep fresh. Use as a scratchpad; move items to Confluence if they become permanent.

Summary (two lines):
- Recent spike in L7 latencies around 02:00 UTC tied to a vswitch incident + autoscaler behavior.
- Temporary mitigations applied: scaled dedicated pool down to stable config; pinned model variant; re-enabled prefix caching on route /v1/generate.

What I saw last shift (timestamps UTC):
- 01:48: first slow increase in p95 token latency on hosted-api/infra-frontend (from 180ms -> 420ms).
- 01:52: error rate for route /v1/generate rose to 0.6% (mostly 503s from model-workers).
- 02:05: autoscaler triggered scale-up of dedicated pool, but new instances spun in with boot-time kernel mismatch (see logs).
- 02:22: applied emergency pin to model-version 2.1.3-quant; error-rate dropped to 0.1%.

Immediate checks for next person (quick checklist):
- Clear: Dashboard -> Hosted API -> Per-route -> /v1/generate (time range 00:00-03:00) -> watch p50/p95 and error-rate.
- Logs: run `rlog service=worker role=model-workers --since 3h --level error | grep -i "kernel"` (search kernel/driver mismatch).
- Autoscaler: `kubectl -n infra get hpa,dv` then `kubectl -n infra describe deployment model-worker`. Look for failing readiness probes.
- Cache: confirm prefix cache hit rate on console (Optimize -> Caching) — target >75% for this route.
- Throttle: if errors >1% and latency >500ms, flip route to dedicated-only via routing policy (console -> routing -> route override).

Temporary mitigation steps I did (do not revert until oncall sync):
- Pinned route /v1/generate to model-version 2.1.3-quant at 02:22.
- Disabled autoscale burst for pool-dedicated-east-1 (flag: autoscale.burst=false) to avoid noisy provisioning.
- Toggled kernel-retry-backoff (infra flag) to 30s from 120s to reduce noisy reboots while we investigate.
- Created INF ticket INF-3421 (linked above).

Why pinned: the 2.2.x variant has an interaction with newer GPU driver produced by node autoscaler images; 2.1.3-quant runs on current nodes reliably. Pinning avoids cascading retries and keeps tail latencies reasonable while infra teams patch image.

Known gaps / TODOs (items I left undone):
- Follow up with infra-release on image rollout plan (owner: Ethan).
- Add explicit healthcheck histogram for worker readiness to the console (owner: SRE-observability).
- Create a small smoke test that sends a 64-token request every 10s to new nodes during scale-up; add to release job.

Quick commands (cheat sheet):
- Check route stats (CLI): `redwoodctl routes stats --route /v1/generate --range 3h`
- Find failing pods: `kubectl -n infra get pods --selector=app=model-worker -o wide`
- Describe problematic pod: `kubectl -n infra describe pod <pod>` then `kubectl -n infra logs <pod> -c worker`
- Force-pull model variant to a healthy node: `redwoodctl model pin --route /v1/generate --version 2.1.3-quant`
- Toggle routing policy: Console -> Deployments -> Routing -> Select route -> “Force route to pool”

Escalation contacts (order):
- Oncall SRE primary (Slack: @ethan.b) — pager if >30m no improvement or production-wide degrade.
- Infra oncall (Slack: #infra-oncall) — for kernel/image issues.
- Product (Maya/PM) — only if customer SLA impact or >2% error-rate sustained.

Notes to self / improvisation log:
- 02:10: observed a pattern of nodes failing readiness after GPU driver update. Suspect kernel module mismatch between curated node image v1.14 and the new node-ami baked last week.
- 02:30: toggled prefix caching back on (it was off due to an unrelated deploy). Hit rate improved immediately — notable reduction in model-worker CPU on tokenization stage.

If you take over (how to proceed):
1) Read INF-3421, check linked infra PR in linked_artifacts.
2) Keep route pinned until infra confirms new image build with driver fix.
3) If you need to open the rollback: run `redwoodctl rollout rollback --deployment model-workers --to 2026-02-26` (last stable image tag).
4) If errors spike again and pin doesn't help, change routing to pass traffic to dedicated-backup pool: console -> routing -> set route to dedicated-backup-east (this will cost more, but preserves latency).

Small heuristics I use (for context):
- If p95 > 3x p50 and errors >0.5% -> look for worker OOMs or busy GC (core dumps show up as OOMKill in pod events).
- If new nodes failing readiness on first 10m -> likely image/kernel mismatch.
- If latencies increase but CPU stays low -> likely network/vswitch or KV cache cold-start.

Post-shift follow-ups I left in the ticket: (short)
- Add smoke test to PR for node-image.
- Add a small Grafana panel for kernel module errors (label: kernel/mismatch).
- Audit autoscaler config for burst thresholds (owner: infra).

Loose thinking / brainstorm (leave here until formalized):
- Could we do a soft-attach staging pool that drains and validates nodes before autoscaler attaches them? Maybe run a short 'warmup' traffic profile to exercise model initialization.
- Consider adding per-model immutable labels for gpu-driver-compat; routing engine could prefer nodes with matching label.

Random notes / snippet for later (copy this into the ticket if useful):
- `journalctl -k | grep -i nvidia` -> showed module taint lines at 01:50.
- `curl -sS http://metrics.internal/prefix-cache/hits?route=/v1/generate` -> improved from 42% -> 79% after enabling.

Anything you touch, please note in this doc (append updates) and add short timestamp + name. If you escalate to a paging incident, write the timeline into INF-3421 and ping me.

-- Maya 2026-03-02 03:14UTC
